clue.text: British scientist consuming new nibbles

indicators.note: a scientist consuming something takes it inside, so the letter goes into the name

parts.note: Oliver Sacks was a British neurologist and author

explanation.surface: A British researcher is caught eating something fresh between meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibbles are light bites eaten between meals, which is what snacks are too; both are plural nouns.

clue.text: Special person in fancy gear is paediatrician

indicators.note: in places the special-person letters inside the reworked letters of gear
fancy as an adjective suggests something elaborate or reworked, so gear's letters are rearranged

parts.note: per means for each person, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: An unusual individual wearing flamboyant clothes turns out to be a children's doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' gives AGER, which 'in' opens after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Asperger was the Austrian children's doctor after whom a form of autism was named.

clue.text: Find woman without daughter favouring active involvement

indicators.note: without tells us the daughter's letter is dropped from the word for a woman

parts.note: a lady is a woman
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
hands-on describes a practical, personally involved approach

explanation.surface: Looking for a woman with no daughter who prefers to get stuck in personally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' looks like part of the story but is the definition, as a verb phrase meaning locate or get hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay hands on something is an idiom for locating or getting hold of it, as when one discovers a lost item.

clue.text: Player's representative snubbed in rugby club

indicators.note: snubbed suggests cut short, like a snub nose, so the final letter is docked

parts.note: a sports player's agent represents them in contracts

explanation.surface: A footballer's agent is given the cold shoulder at a rugby club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' means cut short here, not ignored, so AGENT loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: SU Agen is a professional rugby union club from the town of Agen in south-west France.

clue.text: A relative has endless fizzy drink when entering in this way US city

indicators.note: when entering says the run of pieces goes inside the word for in this way

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
nan is an informal word for a grandmother

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the drink is cut off

parts.note: tonic water is a fizzy mixer drink

explanation.surface: A relative's soft drink goes flat on the way into an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the drink's last letter; 'when entering' places the whole run between the two letters for 'in this way'.
explanation.definitionFit: San Antonio is a large city in Texas, home of the Alamo.

clue.text: Superficial flaw in part of a golfer's repertoire

definitions.meaning: a small nick or broken-off fragment on a surface, as on a mug
a short lofted shot played onto the green from close by

explanation.surface: A small weakness shows up in one of a golfer's shots.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small surface defect and a short lofted approach shot in golf.

clue.text: Key fare includes refined bread of old

indicators.note: includes says the pair of pieces takes the refined letter within them

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
to fare is to get on, as in 'how do you do', so do means fare
U means upper-class, hence refined or posh

explanation.surface: Some important food contains a better-quality loaf from times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, and 'fare' is the verb (how one does), not food.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was Portugal's currency before the euro, so it is money (bread) from the past.

clue.text: Bet name's changed for underground site

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A wager's name is altered for a secret subterranean location.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the storey of a building below ground level.

clue.text: A love for time gone stirring lots again

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the words given are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A fondness for the past stirs up plenty of feeling once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful longing for a past era, a love for bygone days.

clue.text: One receiving guests with a plant

parts.note: a host welcomes guests

explanation.surface: Someone welcoming visitors carries a pot plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostas are leafy perennial garden plants, also called plantain lilies.

clue.text: Pair of revolutionaries taken with nationalist language

indicators.note: pair of says the revolutionary's name is given twice

parts.note: Che Guevara is crosswords' favourite revolutionary

explanation.surface: Two rebels side with a separatist speaker of the local tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Chechen is the Caucasian tongue spoken in Chechnya, a Russian republic with a separatist history.

clue.text: A person assisting dealer keeps postal order for small container

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the order's letters go inside the courier

parts.note: a mule smuggles drugs for a dealer

explanation.surface: A drug courier holds on to a money order, hidden in a tiny vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampoule is a small sealed glass vial for an injectable drug dose.

clue.text: Wind from the east gets to decline

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: gas is flatulence, wind

explanation.surface: An easterly breeze brings a drop in conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or sink, a decline in level or value.

clue.text: Approach taken by man with book in style that's offensively pointed

parts.note: to near is to approach

indicators.note: in places the man and book letters inside the word for style

parts.note: tone means manner or style
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man's way with a book is rather too sharp for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' links, leaving 'offensively pointed' as the adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks that cut close to the bone are near enough to the truth, or the indecent, to give offence.

clue.text: A tense time amid awful frost to an extent

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the tense and time letters go into the mangled frost
awful suggests something botched, so the letters of frost are reshaped

parts.note: T is a grammar abbreviation for tense
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A nervous period in bitter cold conditions, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' gives FSORT, and 'amid' opens it after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'after a sort' means partly or in some fashion, the same as somewhat.

clue.text: European distributed treats, yes, in comfortable situation

indicators.note: distributed means spread about, so the letters given are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A European hands out sweets and says yes, well placed to be generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on easy street is an idiom for living in financial comfort.

clue.text: Man in Latin America has computer problem

parts.note: vir is the Latin for man
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A man in Latin America has trouble with his computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin America' looks like one region, but it splits: 'Man in Latin' is the Latin word, and 'America' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus is malicious code that spreads between machines, a common computing problem.

clue.text: Victor again rejecting a good number on English ship shows conceit

parts.note: V is Victor in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: rejecting says the letters for a and good are turned away from the word again

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A winner once more refuses a fine figure on a British vessel, displaying arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' takes A and G out of AGAIN, leaving AIN; 'shows' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit is excessive pride in oneself, which is what vanity or self-admiration means.

clue.text: Light brown vehicle transporting oil (half obscured)

indicators.note: half obscured means only the first half of the vehicle's name stays visible

parts.note: a tanker carries oil by road or sea

explanation.surface: A pale brown truck carrying petroleum is partly hidden from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Tan is a yellowish-brown colour, like light leather or sun-browned skin.

clue.text: Leave a dish with ice cream

definitions.meaning: to depart, as in 'let's go now', slang for leaving
a banana dessert halved lengthways and served with ice cream

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a bowl of dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for departing and also names the banana dessert served with ice cream.

clue.text: University given right to probe serial offender as university employee

indicators.note: to probe is to go inside, so the university and right letters enter the offender's name

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter is the fictional serial killer of The Silence of the Lambs

explanation.surface: A university, with justice on its side, investigates a repeat criminal on its staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecturer teaches at a university, so is one of its academic staff.

clue.text: Current team sport in African country in blistering sun is out of place

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: this in places the country with its sport inside the scrambled sun
blistering suggests something battered, so the letters of sun are rearranged
in puts the sport's letters inside the African country's name

parts.note: Congo is a country in central Africa
RU stands for rugby union, a team sport

explanation.surface: Playing rugby in Congo's scorching sun seems quite wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blistering' gives NUS; the first 'in' makes CONGRUO, and the second puts that after NUS's N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incongruous is at odds with its setting, so unfitting or inappropriate.

clue.text: Revolutionary protest in Cyprus, something marked by hoots?

indicators.note: in places the turned protest inside Cyprus's code letters

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the protest word is read backwards

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A radical demonstration in Cyprus is greeted with jeering horns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoots' means bursts of laughter, not jeers or car horns.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is entertainment that makes audiences roar with laughter, so it is full of hoots.

clue.text: On a regular basis, crude thing needed for breaks?

indicators.note: on a regular basis means taking every other letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Something rough is routinely required for interruptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' are runs of scoring shots in snooker or billiards, not rests.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooker player uses a long tapered stick to compile scoring runs, called breaks.

clue.text: A complete lot shunning tips for respectable existence

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so those edge letters are dropped from the whole

parts.note: the entirety is the whole lot

indicators.note: tips are ends, so the first and last letters of respectable are taken

explanation.surface: An entire group avoids the edges of a decent way of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips for respectable' gives R and E, which 'shunning' removes from ENTIRETY.
explanation.definitionFit: Entity can mean being or existence itself, as well as a thing that exists.

clue.text: Long-standing rival in mess after slipping around end of game

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the final letter of game
after slipping suggests a jumble, so the letters of in and mess are rearranged
end of means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A long-time opponent finishes in a heap after losing their footing at the game's close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after slipping' gives NEMSIS, and 'around' takes in the E from 'end of game'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is an arch-enemy or old adversary who is never quite beaten.

clue.text: Sensible artisan eats sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the words given hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A sensible craftsman has sandwiches for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sane means of sound mind and so reasonable or sensible.

clue.text: Standard search with no end of calls to get floor covering

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: with no means the following letter is left out of the search word

parts.note: a quest is a search

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of calls

explanation.surface: A routine hunt with the phone silent ends up looking for flooring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of calls' is S, which 'with no' removes from QUEST, giving QUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquet is flooring made of wooden blocks laid in a geometric pattern.

clue.text: Learner in school gets to make slow progress

indicators.note: in places the learner letter inside the group of whales

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A pupil at school only manages to inch forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of whales, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to walk heavily or work steadily and slowly.

clue.text: Media executive enters medical facility in large car

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so the executive's letters go within the facility

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium
ed is short for editor, a newspaper executive

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss is admitted to a clinic in a big car.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedan is the American name for a saloon car, a full-sized passenger vehicle.

clue.text: Wartime leader is vote loser after shenanigans

indicators.note: shenanigans are mischief or trickery, so the letters given are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician who lost the vote did so because of skulduggery.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin D Roosevelt was US president for most of the Second World War.
